Definition: The country's overall cybersecurity preparedness, based on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI). Covers legal measures, technical measures, organisational measures, capacity development, and cooperation. Essential for trust in stored data and digital services.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 gives Malawi a score of 80.42/100 (legal 18.16, technical 16.06, organisational 17.37, capacity development 12.26, cooperation 16.58 of 20 each), reported by ITU and corroborated by two Malawian outlets citing MACRA. This meets the metadata's '80+' score band (Code 5). Note for human review: ITU's own qualitative tier places Malawi in Tier 3 'Establishing', not Tier 1 'Role-modelling' — the metadata's score-to-tier-name mapping does not match ITU's actual (non-linear) tiering, though the numeric code is unaffected.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Value Name: Comprehensive requirements for personal data or broad categories
Comments: Data Protection Act restricts cross-border transfers §§38-40
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: Read the actual Act text: sections 38-40 of the Data Protection Act 2024 set conditions for CROSS-BORDER TRANSFER of personal data (adequacy assessment, consent, binding corporate rules) — this is not a data localisation mandate requiring storage within Malawi. CMS/Mondaq's Africa Data Protection Guide (May 2025) states explicitly for Malawi: 'there are no data localisation requirements', only a duty to inform data subjects of transfers abroad. The original score conflated transfer-restriction with localisation; revised to Value Code 1 (No data localisation requirements).

Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
Value Name: No government data center or cloud strategy
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: Evidence contradicts 'no government data centre or cloud strategy'. Malawi has operated a National Data Centre in Blantyre since 2022 (Ministry of Information and Digitalisation, ESCOM, Huawei), and a second Tier III Government Data Centre in Lilongwe is nearing completion (commissioning expected mid-2025), per Times Group (Apr 2025) and the World Bank's Digital Malawi Acceleration Project appraisal (2025). A formal national cloud strategy/National Data Strategy is still being developed under that project, not yet adopted, so a fully-fledged G-Cloud strategy is not yet in place. Revised to Value Code 3 (Basic government data centre operational).
